prompt: A characteristic of a sole proprietorship is that the owner
explanation: Receives all the profit. This is a characteristic of a sole proprietorship. Since there is only one person involved in the business, the amount of available money is usually limited to what the owner has or can borrow. The owner cannot transfer all the risk and assumes many of the losses. The owner may need to perform all, or most of, the functions—particularly if s/he cannot afford to hire trained workers.

prompt: A hairstylist cutting a client's hair is an example of a __________ distribution channel.
explanation: Producer to consumer. When a service provider performs an activity for a client (e.g., hairstylists), this is a direct channel of distribution. All of the other alternatives involve one or more intermediaries between the producer and the consumer. These are examples of indirect channels of distribution.

prompt: The Clayton Act of 1914 was enacted to resolve legal issues related to
explanation: Competitive behavior. The Clayton Act makes it illegal to charge different prices to different wholesalers for the same good or service. It also made it illegal to require a customer to purchase a second good or service in order to receive the first. The Clayton Act does not deal with consumer protection, product safety, or environmental behavior.

prompt: Why is it important for a chain of beauty salons to coordinate distribution with its promotional activities?
choices: To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items
To establish a relationship with one intermediary
To charge higher prices for delivery service
To arrange the most economical method of transportation
explanation: To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items. Chains of beauty salons coordinate distribution with their promotional activities in order to make sure that sufficient quantities of items are available when they are advertised. If a chain plans to promote a certain item or offer it at a special price, the chain must make sure that an adequate supply will be on hand to meet consumer demand. Chains may lose customers if they advertise items that are not available because they failed to make the necessary distribution plans. Chains do not coordinate distribution with promotional activities in order to charge higher prices for delivery service, arrange the most economical method of transportation, or establish a relationship with one intermediary.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of an effective persuasive message:
explanation: Creates desire. A persuasive message is intended to change a person's mind or to convince someone to take action. For the message to be effective, it should create a desire in the person to do what the message wants. It should present a good reason or potential benefit that will persuade the reader. Otherwise, there may be no incentive for the person to do what the message wants. Persuasive messages often are assertive, but they should not be aggressive. Persuasive messages do not describe a process or summarize an issue.

prompt: An example of a type of simple written report used in business services marketing is the __________ report.
explanation: Progress. The purpose of a progress report is to give a brief explanation of the status of an activity or project. Business services managers often want frequent updates about activities in their departments, and the progress report is intended to provide that information. Research reports and annual reports usually are long, complex reports that provide a great deal of information and often include supplemental materials.

prompt: The main reason why it is important for service businesses to be ethical in communicating information about their services is to avoid
explanation: Disappointing customers. Businesses should be ethical when communicating information about their services to customers and not make unrealistic promises or misrepresent the benefits or quality of the services. If service businesses misrepresent themselves and are not able to deliver what they promise, customers will be disappointed and perhaps angry. Service businesses that are unethical in communicating to customers often create a negative image of themselves and eventually lose customers who are disappointed because their expectations were not met. Being unethical in communicating information does not necessarily result in being sued or regulated. Unethical communication would not confuse employees, although it may irritate or frustrate them because they must deal with customers' disappointment or anger.

prompt: An aspect of human relations that has become very important to many service businesses is
explanation: Positive attitudes toward customers. Many service businesses have determined that treating customers well and providing good service are very important to the success of the business. The varieties of products offered by the business, the demographics of its target market, and the convenience of its location are also important, but they are not aspects of human relations.

prompt: In a service business, what staff are responsible for displaying a customer-service mindset?
explanation: All staff. The customer-service mindset applies to all employees regardless of whether they ever come into direct contact with customers. It takes all staff focused on customer satisfaction to convince customers that a business is sincerely interested in them. For example, a lawyer's efforts to determine and satisfy a client's needs must be supported by all other staff members in the law firm.

prompt: What type of customer may be haughty or overbearing to an employee?
explanation: Domineering/Superior. These customers are overly confident and feel that they know more and are better than the average person. They will often behave in an arrogant manner toward employees. Suspicious customers question everything and may want facts and proof before being convinced that something is true. Dishonest customers intentionally attempt to avoid paying for the good or service by deceiving the salesperson. Slow/Methodical customers require a lot of time to make a purchase because of shyness or difficulty in making a choice or buying decision.

prompt: When helping disagreeable customers, it is best for a business-services employee to
choices: try to talk louder than they.
explanation: Serve them promptly. It is best to try to serve disagreeable customers as promptly as possible. By serving them promptly, you decrease the chances that they will become more disagreeable. You also build goodwill for the service business. You should compliment or praise the domineering/superior customer. No customer should feel pressured into making buying decisions. You should speak softly when working with difficult customers rather than trying to talk louder than they.

prompt: Josh and Ann operate a health care business and are considering expanding by selling franchises. Franchising their service would allow them to
choices: provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image.
secure their financial future by collecting royalties.
explanation: Provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image. A franchise is a type of service intermediary. Franchises for service businesses are increasing due to the desire to provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image and level of quality. Offering franchises would not allow them to control the prices of competitors or increase inventory or storage control. Collecting franchise fees and royalties may enhance their financial future, but it does not secure it as other variables may come into play.

prompt: If a desired good or service is scarce, consumers will usually be
choices: able to get as much of it as they want.
explanation: Willing to pay more. A good or service is considered scarce when not everyone can have as much of it as desired. This makes consumers willing to pay for the item in order to obtain it. Since scarce items may be hard to locate, consumers may be more interested in owning them and willing to buy them.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why form utility is so important:
choices: Few materials are used in their raw state.
Consumers use the products they purchase.
Most products are marketed at a certain time.
Products must be available where they are needed.
explanation: Few materials are used in their raw state. Form utility occurs when a business alters or changes the shape or form of a product to make it more useful to consumers. Form utility is important because very few materials are used in their raw form. Businesses need to change the shapes or forms of materials so that they will be useful to consumers. Products' being available where they are needed is place utility. Products' being marketed at a certain time is time utility. Consumers' using the products they purchase is possession utility.

prompt: What usually happens to the demand for a good or service when the price increases?
explanation: It decreases. People may wait for lower prices; switch to a substitute item, if one is available; or decide not to buy at all, if they think prices are too high. When prices increase, demand usually decreases rather than increasing or staying the same. Demand would not come to an end, because some people will still buy.

prompt: Government tries to protect competition by
choices: restricting the production of certain products.
explanation: Regulating monopolies. A monopoly is a business that influences the entire production of a particular good or service. Controlling product prices and restricting production of certain products are actions that monopolies can take to increase product prices. The government does not prevent all forms of monopolies since it allows natural monopolies—monopolies that are in the best interest of the public.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of taxes:
explanation: Levied by governments. Taxes are levied by various levels of government for different reasons. One reason is to generate revenue to fund programs. All levels of government, from small cities to the national level, need money to operate. They obtain this money by levying taxes on individuals and businesses. Taxes are not restricted to businesses or applied only to tangibles. Although consumers pay taxes, they usually do not encourage additional taxes.

prompt: A country's economy grows when its population grows at a slower rate than its
explanation: GDP per capita. GDP (gross domestic product) per capita is the average productivity of individual workers calculated by dividing the gross domestic product by the worker hours required to produce it. When a country's GDP per capita grows at a faster rate than its population, the country's economy can grow. The standard of living is affected by productivity. Management should improve workers' quality of work life to help to increase productivity. Capital goods are manufactured or constructed items that are used to produce goods and services.

prompt: Workers in your landscape design company have decided to join a union. As a member of management, which form of union representation will you encourage?
explanation: Open shop. Open shops are preferred by management since it permits them to discourage new employees from joining the union, thus limiting the union's bargaining power. In union shops, employees are required to join unions after their probationary period. In closed shops, prospective employees must belong to unions before the company can hire them. Closed shops are illegal in all states. In agency shops, all employees are required to pay union dues but do not have to join the union.

prompt: When applying the law of diminishing returns, service businesses know that there is a point at which production
explanation: Reaches its maximum level. The law of diminishing returns states that, at some point, adding more resources does not proportionately increase productivity. For example, adding more employees when there is limited space and equipment will eventually have a negative effect on production because overcrowding will occur, and no one will be able to work efficiently. Service businesses apply this law when deciding whether to hire more employees or purchase more materials and equipment. All of the resources need to be compatible for production to reach its maximum level. Once maximum production occurs, adding more resources will begin to diminish the rate of productivity. The law of diminishing returns does not determine at which point production is too expensive to continue, equals the amount of revenue, or passes that of the competition.

prompt: What is one way that price stability indicates the condition of the economy?
explanation: Absence of inflation or deflation. When prices are stable, there are no large changes in prices either up or down. This means that prices are fairly constant. Price stability is an indication of the condition of the economy because when prices are stable, the economy is stable. Therefore, inflation and deflation do not occur. Inflation is a rapid rise in prices and deflation is a rapid decrease in prices. Price stability does not necessarily mean there is a reduction in taxes and spending, an increase in the money supply, or a decrease in consumer buying power.

prompt: One step that a government might take to reduce its trade deficit would be to
explanation: Adjust interest rates. A trade deficit is an unfavorable balance of trade in which a nation's imports are greater than its exports. Nations use several techniques to reduce their trade deficits, including adjusting interest rates to keep investments at home. Favorable interest rates encourage businesses to invest their profits in their own countries. Increasing the amount of imports, eliminating tariffs, and decreasing the amount of exports probably would increase a nation's trade deficit.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a service business that is most likely to experience demand fluctuations for some services due to unpredictable events:
explanation: Insurance agency. Many business organizations have a difficult time predicting or forecasting the demand for their services. For example, an insurance agency that sells homeowners' insurance might experience unexpected increases in insurance claims when a natural disaster (e.g., hurricane, tornado, flood) causes widespread damage to business and residential areas. Since natural disasters are unpredictable events, insurance service needs are affected. Although services related to hospital emergency rooms might be affected by unpredictable events, most surgical outpatient clinics maintain surgery schedules. Therefore, demand for surgical services is not generally affected by unpredictable events. A computer distributor sells tangible items rather than services. Tax returns have specific due dates, which makes the demand cycle for tax accounting services more predictable.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a service-business employee developing cultural sensitivity:
choices: Taking a course in ancient history
Studying road maps of various countries
explanation: Learning differences in body language. Body language includes gestures, facial expressions, tone of voice, or any other form of communicating without words. These forms of nonverbal communication have different meanings in different parts of the world. Furthermore, some gestures that are acceptable in one country are actually offensive in other countries. Service-business employees who take the time to learn the differences in body language usually are able to develop cultural sensitivity and avoid using inappropriate gestures and facial expressions. Service-business employees do not develop cultural sensitivity by practicing oral presentation skills, taking a course in ancient history, or studying road maps of various countries.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a manager being unethical when communicating with an architecture firm's employees:
choices: Explaining that some information is confidential
Sending information in simple chart form
Deliberately limiting the distribution of classified information
explanation: Deliberately providing insufficient information. In some situations, a manager might deliberately provide insufficient information for the purpose of setting up an employee to fail. This is considered an unethical way to communicate because the employee does not have a fair chance to complete an assignment successfully. Managers have an obligation to treat all employees ethically and give them the information and tools needed to do the job. It is ethical for managers to explain that some information is confidential and to limit the distribution of classified information. Sending information in simple chart form often makes it easier for employees to understand complex data.

prompt: Pedro, an employee with a local law firm, wants to negotiate with his supervisor to gain more responsibilities at work. Before approaching his supervisor, Pedro needs to determine the supervisor's position and
explanation: Interests. The key to successful negotiation is to focus on interests. Interests are the things that each person wants or needs. Pedro must consider his superior's interests as well as his own. Skill is the ability to perform a task through knowledge, training, and practice. When negotiating, one person may not necessarily know the other person's skills. Standards are specifications or statements that are used as a basis for comparing or judging goods or services. A procedure is the step-by-step process someone follows when performing a specific task.

prompt: On the whole, consensus building is about
explanation: Coming to an agreement. On the whole, consensus building is about coming to an agreement. It's not about determining a place to meet, though that may be helpful. It's not supposed to be about putting aside your beliefs, though compromise may be encouraged. And, developing ground rules is a good practice for group activities, but it is not the overall meaning of consensus building.

prompt: When an apparel store's customer is permitted to pay his/her credit account in full in 30 days, or make a minimum payment and be charged a finance charge on the balance, s/he has a(n) __________ account.
explanation: Revolving. Customers with revolving credit accounts can avoid finance charges by paying the balance due on the account by the end of each 30-day period. There is usually a limit on the total amount of the customer's monthly charges. Cycle billing determines the dates customers receive statements. Regular credit requires balances to be paid in full each month. Installment credit requires a down payment and payments at regular intervals.

prompt: Which of the following enables many service businesses to obtain the funds needed to reach new markets:
explanation: Financing. Financing is the process of determining the need for and availability of financial resources for a business. Many service businesses may need the money they have on hand for everyday operations and may need to borrow additional funds in order to expand and reach new markets. Financing makes it possible for service businesses to grow and prosper. Budgeting is the process of estimating and allocating funds to cover expenses. Purchasing involves obtaining goods and services for use in the business. Accounting is the process of keeping financial records.

prompt: Carpet-cleaning businesses are able to deposit employees' salaries directly into their checking accounts through the use of
explanation: Electronic funds transfer. Electronic funds transfer (EFT) makes it possible to move money from one account to another by computer. Many businesses (e.g., carpet-cleaning businesses) use EFT to deposit employees' salaries directly into their checking accounts. The bank automatically subtracts the amount of payroll from the business's account and deposits the correct amount into each employee's account. This technology also enables the bank to make deposits to employees' accounts that are with other banks. Electronic funds transfer makes employees' salaries available immediately upon deposit and eliminates the need for payroll checks. Businesses are not able to deposit employees' salaries directly into their checking account through the use of telegraphic money orders, automated teller machines, or money-market processing.

prompt: Buying insurance is one way that engineering businesses manage
explanation: Risk. Insurance is a contractual agreement in which one company (insurer) will pay for specified losses incurred by the other company (insured) in return for installment payments (premiums). Engineering businesses buy insurance to manage risk, which is the possibility of loss or failure. Insurance protects the business from many types of risk, such as property damage. For example, if a business facility is vandalized, insurance will pay for the repairs. Coverage is the amount an insurance company will pay for a loss. Injury and damage are types of risk for which businesses can buy insurance.

prompt: What is one of the main purposes of a pet-grooming business's sales budget?
explanation: To estimate income. The sales budget sets the financial pace for a pet-grooming business by estimating what amount of expenses and income can be expected from the sale of the business's services. Sales budgets are extremely important because they estimate the major source of income, which helps a pet-grooming business determine if it will be profitable. Businesses take into consideration future trends, the state of the economy, and the level of competition when developing their sales budgets.

prompt: Excise taxes that are collected by service businesses are paid by them to the __________ government.
explanation: Federal. Service businesses must collect, report, and pay to the appropriate government a variety of taxes. Excise taxes are a type of sales tax on selected products and are paid to the federal government. General sales taxes are paid to city, county, and/or state governments.

prompt: A service business had gross sales of $14,959 and tax-exempt sales of $1,628. What is the amount of sales on which the service business must report sales tax?
explanation: $13,331. Tax exempt sales are those on which sales tax is not charged. The amount of tax exempt sales is, therefore, subtracted from gross sales in reporting and paying sales tax to the government. In this case, $14,959 - $1,628 = $13,331.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a landscaping company transferring the charges on a member's account:
choices: Recording the charges on a computer system
Moving the charges to a monthly bill
Forwarding the charges to accounts payable
Assigning the charges to a certain department
explanation: Moving the charges to a monthly bill. Some landscaping companies bill their members on a monthly basis. During the month, the customer's charges for certain activities are recorded on the member's account. At the end of the month, the charges are transferred to the billing statement which is sent to the customer for payment. The customer's account now indicates that the billing period has ended and the charges are listed as receivables. Accounts payable are the monies the landscaping business owes to others rather than the monies owed to it by customers. Assigning charges to a certain department or recording charges on a computer system are not examples of transferring charges on a customer's account.

prompt: What does a home improvement business need in order to understand why a service that has been in demand for a long time is now losing popularity?
explanation: Marketing information. Marketing information is all of the marketing-related data available inside and outside the home improvement business. This includes information about customers, competitors, demographics, etc. Home improvement services need marketing information in order to understand why the demand for a service that has been strong for a long time is now losing popularity. For example, marketing information might tell a home improvement business that the target market for outdoor decks is decreasing in size because more people want patios and sun porches. Once the home improvement business understands the reason for the loss in popularity, it can take steps to correct the problem. These steps may include adding patios and/or sun porches to its product line. Sales records are a type of marketing information, but they usually indicate only the decrease in sales rather than the reason for the decrease. Secondary data is a type of marketing information that has been collected for purposes other than the project at hand. It may not be useful in determining why a product is now losing popularity. Purchasing documents are documents a business uses to purchase goods and services.

prompt: Evaluating the information collected through market research is called
explanation: Data analysis. Data analysis may include comparisons with other data or presentation of the data in different formats. Primary data are facts collected specifically for the problem or project at hand. Information flow is the process of moving information through the appropriate channels or making information accessible to those who need it. Risk reduction is a business's efforts to reduce or control its exposure to risk.

prompt: Marketing research is used in problem solving and decision making in all areas of the marketing mix which includes
explanation: Promotion. Promotion is a marketing function which communicates information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. Promotion is one of the "Ps" in the marketing mix. The other elements of the marketing mix are product, place, and price. Productivity and persuasion are not areas of the marketing mix. Personal selling is a component of the promotional mix.

prompt: What is one way that many service businesses use the marketing information contained in sales reports?
choices: To improve the effectiveness of salespeople
explanation: To improve the effectiveness of salespeople. Sales reports contain a variety of marketing information that service businesses often use to improve the effectiveness of salespeople. This includes information about number of new customers, number of lost customers, cost of selling, time spent with each customer, etc. By reviewing the information, a business can determine if the salesperson is effective, or might need assistance or more training to be better able to market the business's products to customers. For example, a sales call report might reveal that customers want detailed product information that the salesperson does not have. Then, the business can develop materials to provide the detailed information. This will help the salesperson to more effectively work with customers. Businesses do not use the marketing information contained in sales reports to qualify potential new customers or to develop negotiating techniques. Expense accounts are types of sales reports that often contain marketing information.

prompt: One reason it is important to review paper-based questionnaires before processing the marketing information is because some of the questionnaires may be
explanation: Improperly filled out and unusable. Paper-based questionnaires and surveys are often used to obtain marketing information from customers. However, businesses that use paper-based questionnaires should physically review them to be sure that they are completed properly. If the questionnaires are improperly filled out, they may be unusable because the information is incorrect or not readable. For example, if customers leave some spaces blank or fill in more than one response to a question, those questionnaires may need to be discarded because the answers are not valid and will affect the accuracy of the research. Many questionnaires contain answer codes that only researchers are able to read and understand. Most questionnaires are completed anonymously; therefore, they are not organized according to last name.

prompt: Databases assist consulting businesses in decision making because they
choices: organize and store data in a logical order for fast and easy use.
create charts, graphs, unbound reports, and simplified memos.
increase operational budgets of technology related departments.
determine open-to-buy, ROI, and CPM accurately.
explanation: Organize and store data in a logical order for fast and easy use. Consulting businesses collect many forms of data each day by a variety of means. This data can then be used by decision makers to guide their choices. Databases help to organize the information so that it can be used most efficiently. The alternatives are not reasons why a database would assist in decision making.

prompt: The first step that an architecture firm should take when collecting marketing information from its clients is to
explanation: Define research objectives. Before collecting marketing data, an architecture firm must define the problem or objective of the research. Once the researchers know why they are collecting the information, they can determine where and how to collect it. Marketing research is not always obtained through surveys or secondary data sources. Rating scales are often developed to measure or qualify research results. Rating scales are generally developed after the research objectives are determined.

prompt: A dental office that focuses its marketing efforts on attracting children to its practice by promoting its kid-friendly staff is engaged in __________ marketing.
explanation: Target. Target marketing refers to the identification and selection of markets for a business or for a product. In this case, the market happens to be children who might benefit from a kid-friendly staff. Business-to-business marketing occurs when one business focuses its marketing efforts on another business. An example in the dental industry would be a drill manufacturer that tries to sell its products to a dentist. When target markets are clearly defined, marketing tends to be less risky because advertising can provide specific information about the benefits the targeted group can expect to receive from the service. The dental office is focused (as opposed to unfocused) on attracting a specific market (i.e., children) to its practice.

prompt: Which of the following terms refers to the activities involved in shipping, handling, and storing items on the way from the producer to the consumer:
explanation: Distribution. Distribution involves moving, storing, locating, and/or transferring ownership of goods and services. The distribution activities ensure that items are available when and where they are needed. Warehousing is only one aspect of distribution. In turn, distribution is only one of the activities that make up the marketing process. Economics is the study of how to satisfy unlimited, competing wants with limited resources.

prompt: Which of the following is least likely to necessitate a change in marketing strategies:
choices: Increases in the cost of production
explanation: Increases in company profits. Increased profits would indicate that the company's marketing strategies are successful and not currently in need of change. Factors that may prompt a business to change marketing strategies include the actions of competitors and suppliers, increases in the cost of production, the influences of governmental agencies, and changes in consumer attitudes. Marketing strategies should be designed so that they are flexible enough to accommodate changes as needed.

prompt: When a customer has an unfulfilled desire and is financially able and willing to satisfy that desire, a ________ exists.
explanation: Market. A market is a particular group of consumers who want or need a given good or service. A market cannot exist unless customers who have desires for products can also afford to buy them. A monopoly is a market situation in which there is only one supplier of a certain good or service, and no substitute is readily available. A society is a group of individuals who share an environment. A business is an organized effort to produce and/or distribute goods and services.

prompt: Why is it important for home security businesses to regularly analyze the external environment in which they operate?
explanation: To understand change. Home security businesses need to understand changes in their external environment in order to adapt and remain competitive. To do this, they often conduct situational analyses to gather information about changes or trends that are beginning to develop in the environment or marketplace. This procedure allows businesses to identify changes at an early stage and decide if they present a threat to the way the business is currently operating. Businesses do not analyze their external environment in order to be socially responsible, behave ethically, or calculate profit.

prompt: Which of the following factors affects how far ahead a service business needs to predict its sales:
choices: The typical information that is available
The productivity of the service business
explanation: The service business's resources. A service business that is short of operating funds could use a short-term forecast in order to determine whether sales income will be enough to cover operating expenses. A service business that has plenty of financial resources can afford to prepare a longer term sales forecast. Other factors that affect how far ahead a service business needs to predict its sales are the objectives of the business, the purpose(s) of the forecast, and the conditions of the market. The choice of forecasting methods is affected by the type of information that is available. The productivity of the service business affects the level at which the sales forecast will be set. Changes in the number of competitors or in their marketing strategies may require that sales forecasts be adjusted. However, the similarity of competitors does not affect the selection of a timeframe for forecasting sales.

prompt: A good customer database makes it possible for a service business to
explanation: Predict trends. By monitoring a customer database, a service business is able to track the type of goods customers are buying and how much they are spending. It will tell them if customers are spending more or less and if they are affected by seasonal and price changes. Therefore, these data help service businesses predict future trends. As a result of identifying trends, a service business might decide to offer better discounts. An existing customer database will not help a service business find new customers or calculate profits.

prompt: What is one reason that a landscaping business might make its financial records available to a bank?
explanation: To obtain credit. Businesses keep records to verify information for others. For example, if a landscaping business wishes to obtain a loan from a bank, it must provide the bank with financial records to prove that it is creditworthy. The financial records provide information about the landscaping business's income and expenses and verify that the business will be able to repay the loan. Businesses only need to deposit funds in order to open an account with a bank. A landscaping business that is paying a mortgage already has received a loan.

prompt: Most lawn-care businesses maintain records about what services customers are buying and how much they are spending in order to
explanation: Analyze the information. Most lawn-care businesses maintain customer records that contain information about what services customers are buying, when they are buying them, and how much they are spending. By analyzing this information, lawn-care businesses are able to plan future sales and provide the services that will appeal to customers and encourage them to buy. Without this type of information, lawn-care businesses might have no idea what customers will want to buy in the future or how much they will be willing to spend. Lawn-care businesses do not maintain records about what customers are buying and how much they are spending in order to plan an inventory count, assess their fixed assets, or develop a quality work environment.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to consumers of the trend towards franchising in the business-service industry:
explanation: Service is consistent. Franchising is a method of distributing goods and services through a licensing arrangement between the franchisor and franchisee. The advantage of franchising is that the service is consistent because of procedures required by the franchisor. This benefits consumers because they know they will receive the same service from all franchises. Franchising does not guarantee that the business will be profitable. Although the business-service industry is diversified, that is not necessarily a benefit to consumers. Promotion is often regionalized rather than global.

prompt: For safety's sake, pet groomers learning new skills should take the time to practice the skills and avoid taking
explanation: Shortcuts. Pet groomers learning new skills should practice the new skill using the appropriate steps rather than taking shortcuts. It is important to practice a new skill slowly and cautiously because the quickest way is not necessarily the safest way. Not taking shortcuts is an important safety procedure that helps protect pet groomers and their customers' pets from many accidents and injuries. Learning new skills should not interfere with taking vacations, rest breaks, and personal leave.

prompt: A dry cleaner's employees should follow set policies for accepting personal checks and credit cards in order to prevent
explanation: Point-of-sale fraud. Attempts to cheat a business (e.g., dry cleaner) out of money at the time of purchase is point-of-sale fraud. To prevent point-of-sale fraud, employees should be familiar with the types of fraud associated with credit cards, checks, and cash. Businesses usually have detailed steps for employees to follow in accepting checks and credit cards. Ticket switching is a type of fraud in which a higher priced ticket is removed from merchandise and replaced by a lower priced ticket. Internal theft is any kind of theft by employees of the business. Recordkeeping fraud involves altering business records and diverting money.

prompt: Which of the following should an architecture firm consider when developing a project plan to help control costs:
explanation: Potential problems. An effective project plan helps to control costs by considering potential problems that may arise. By addressing problems in the planning stage, an architecture firm is able to develop a method of dealing with potential problems, which often eliminates the need to make costly changes while completing the project. Architecture firms establish the objectives before developing the plan to carry out the project. Publicity is free, although many projects are internal and do not involve publicity. Furthermore, not all projects are intended to be advertised, so advertising expense is not always involved.

prompt: Three-way light bulbs are all made with the same size base. This is an example of a production process that uses __________ parts.
explanation: Standardized. Some production processes, such as mass production, use standardized parts to make large quantities of similar products. Standardized parts are interchangeable. Grading is the process of rating products according to certain established standards or characteristics. Branding is the ongoing decision-making process about the use of brands. Segmenting divides people or things into sections according to certain criteria.

prompt: What are dry cleaners often faced with if their employees improperly handle company equipment?
explanation: Additional expenses. Repairing or replacing damaged or broken equipment is often costly for dry cleaners. Most dry cleaners budget a certain amount each year for routine maintenance and repair and for scheduled replacement of old equipment. Mishandled equipment often needs to be repaired or replaced before expected, which involves an additional expense for the dry cleaner. The need for maintenance usually increases if employees improperly handle company equipment. Vandalism is the willful or malicious destruction of property. Dry cleaners whose employees improperly handle company equipment may establish more company regulations in an attempt to correct the problem.

prompt: Which of the following is an area in a medical office that must be maintained on a regular basis:
explanation: Floor surfaces. The floor is a major area of most medical offices and is one regularly used by patients. Whether the floor surface is carpeted or tiled, it should be maintained in good condition. Patients may trip and fall on torn carpet or loose pieces of tile. Properly maintaining all floor surfaces helps to prevent injury to patients and employees and presents an orderly image of the office. Ceiling fans, table lamps, and wall mirrors are types of accessories and equipment rather than areas in an office.

prompt: Which of the following procedures would be the best for a car rental agency to implement in order to reduce check losses:
choices: Develop a profile of a bad-check writer
Write the customer's description on the check
explanation: Use a check verification service. This type of service, such as TeleCheck, maintains a national database and makes check verification quick and fairly inexpensive. This would be the business's best method of reducing bad-check loss. Accepting only local checks would not necessarily reduce bad-check loss. Writing the customer's description on the check is not effective. Car rental agencies do not have the ability to develop a profile of a bad-check writer.

prompt: Which of the following tasks is a cashier's responsibility just prior to the opening of the service-business facility:
explanation: Preparing the checkout area. An opening cashier is responsible for tidying and organizing the checkout area. This ensures that s/he will be ready to offer customers efficient service. Handling customer complaints and answering their questions are possible cashier responsibilities while the business is in operation. If required, the cashiers complete the sales tally sheet at the end of their shifts.

prompt: It is important to develop a personal plan of action for goals because
choices: goals cannot be achieved without a plan.
a plan helps you to achieve your goals.
you can share the plan with others.
explanation: A plan helps you to achieve your goals. With a personal plan of action, you will have a written, step-by-step method of achieving your goal, not just a vague idea of something you desire. However, not even a written plan can guarantee success in reaching goals. It is possible to achieve goals without having a written plan. It is not necessary to share the plan with others.

prompt: Tia has many interests and doesn't know which career path is best for her. One method Tia can use to determine the best occupational options for her is to
choices: surf the Internet for job descriptions.
have friends and family critique her personality type.
explanation: Complete an aptitude assessment survey. Many people have a difficult time selecting a career path that is right for them. Some people complete professionally developed aptitude assessment surveys to help them determine their aptitudes and skills. By considering factors such as personality type, abilities, interests, and learning style, a person can use the survey results to determine the career for which s/he is best suited. Although constructive input from friends and family might help Tia in assessing her career options, the information may not provide her with the objectivity and the detail she would receive from a professionally developed assessment survey. Developing a general interest questionnaire and surfing the Internet for job descriptions are not activities that will provide her with guidance in terms of career selection.

prompt: Chris was interested in a job that was being advertised, but the ad did not provide instructions on whom to contact at the business. What should Chris do in order to send a letter of application?
choices: Call to find out who will make the hiring decision
Address the letter "To whom it may concern"
Ask the newspaper who submitted the job ad
Send the letter to the human resources department
explanation: Call to find out who will make the hiring decision. If the ad does not provide the name of an individual or department to whom inquiries should be addressed, the job seeker should telephone the business to obtain the name of the person who will be making the hiring decision. This is the person to whom the job seeker should explain why s/he is a viable candidate for the position. Not all businesses are large enough to have a human resources department. Addressing the letter "To whom it may concern" would not ensure that the letter would reach the appropriate person. The newspaper would not give out information about its customers.

prompt: Which of the following techniques do businesses often use during trade shows to obtain customers' names:
explanation: Contests. Many businesses conduct contests during trade shows in order to obtain the names and addresses of potential customers. Businesses record the names of people who register for the contests and then send them follow-up information after the trade shows end. A coupon is a certificate entitling the holder to a reduced purchase price. A sample is a small size of a product. A rebate is a return of part of the price a customer pays for a good or service.

prompt: Which of the following traits are most important for health care employees to have in the workplace:
explanation: Empathy and responsiveness. Health care businesses generally require personal contact with their customers. Empathy is the ability to put yourself in another person's place. Responsive refers to the ability to acknowledge and accommodate a customer's needs and wants. When communicating with customers, successful health care employees demonstrate many traits and skills, including being empathetic; responsive; reliable; and, most often, friendly. Although flexibility is often important, the degree of flexibility that a health care employee exhibits is highly dependent on the job or position. Wit (humor) is not always necessary or appropriate. Employees should strive to be assertive, rather than passive or aggressive.

prompt: The owners of a dry-cleaning business decided to ignore the low prices offered by a new competitor and keep their prices at a higher level. What characteristic of effective pricing were the owners forgetting?
explanation: Flexibility. The owners of the dry-cleaning business were forgetting that prices must be flexible, that they are not written in stone. Dry-cleaning businesses need to be willing to adjust their prices depending on the circumstances faced by the business. If a competitor is offering lower prices on similar products, a dry-cleaning business should be flexible with its pricing in order to keep its customers. Durability is how long a product will last. Profitability is the degree or level of profit of a business or a product. Stability is resistance to change.

prompt: Most businesses feel that it is a good strategy to price their service products according to the
choices: agreements set with other channel members.
way their customers view the products.
explanation: Way their customers view the products. Consumers' perceptions of the value received for the price may determine whether or not they buy the products. It is illegal for channel members to make agreements that set prices of products. Many state laws prohibit the sale of loss leaders—products priced below cost. Although a business often considers its competitors' pricing, the business would not take its competitors' suggestions to set pricing.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of pure services:
choices: Does not include a tangible product
explanation: Does not include a tangible product. Services are intangible products that people perform rather than produce, such as a manicure or lawn care. Pure services are groups of services provided to consumers without the involvement of any tangible product. Tangible products rather than intangible products (services) use packaging. Pure services do not always include product guarantees or use product-bundling strategies.

prompt: Ethical repair shops establish procedures to handle consumer complaints and returns.
choices: True, establishing procedures is a way of explaining problems with products because of improper use by customers.
False, establishing procedures is not important unless required by law.
False, establishing procedures is a waste of time if products have been tested for safe use.
True, establishing procedures reduces harmful effects to the shop and its image.
explanation: True, establishing procedures reduces harmful effects to the shop and its image. Not only is it ethical to have procedures for handling complaints and returns, it is also in the best interest of the repair shop. However, these procedures are not required by law. Ethical repair shops want to resolve any problems and provide safe products to customers. Ethical repair shops do not blame customers for problems or believe that procedures are a waste of time or not important.

prompt: Consulting firms often identify product opportunities by conducting
explanation: Trend research. Identifying product opportunities often involves research. One type of research is trend research to find out the general direction in which people or events are moving. For example, trend research might indicate that people want additional services or certain information available for purchase. As a result of trend research, consulting firms are often able to identify product opportunities. Once the opportunity is identified, businesses usually analyze the idea. If the idea is feasible, the businesses may conduct tests.

prompt: What is one of the first steps that businesses take when planning what type of new service to offer?
explanation: Identifying growth opportunities. Before developing a new service, businesses usually examine the market and identify growth opportunities. For example, an insurance company might analyze customers in a certain part of the country to decide if it would be profitable to offer a new type of coverage. If the company finds that there is a sizeable market for that type of coverage, it would proceed with the development. Service businesses realize that there is no point to offering a new service if there is no demand for it. Once a business develops a new service, it often tests it in specific areas. Once the service is made available, businesses promote the idea to customers and continually monitor the service for any needed changes.

prompt: Any business that transports goods across state lines must comply with standards set by
explanation: Government agencies. Government agencies develop standards that usually apply to goods and services that the government regulates. The U.S. Department of Commerce establishes standards for activities such as interstate commerce and transportation. Any business that transports goods across state lines must comply with these government standards. Not all businesses will set interstate transportation standards. Trade associations and professional organizations often establish standards for their members; however, not all businesses belong to these groups.

prompt: Which of the following prohibits service businesses from harassing their slow-pay credit customers:
explanation: Fair Debt Collection Act. The Fair Debt Collection Act is a federal law passed in 1980 prohibiting businesses from harassing or abusing consumers who owe them money. It is one of several laws that relate to consumer credit protection. The Equal Credit Opportunity Act prohibits businesses from engaging in discrimination practices when granting credit to consumers. The Consumer Credit Protection Act requires businesses to disclose their annual interest rates to consumers. The Federal Trade Commission Act established the Federal Trade Commission.

prompt: Which of the following is a possible advantage to service businesses that bundle their products:
explanation: Long-term customer use. Product bundling is the practice of putting together a number of goods/services to create a one-price package, which is less expensive for the customer than purchasing the products individually. A possible advantage to businesses that bundle products is that it often leads to long-term customer use, particularly services such as digital services that are bundled—cable, telephone, and Internet. Low prices and more choices are customer benefits rather than business advantages. When a business experiences cost increases, it is a disadvantage to the business.

prompt: Why are customer-defined service standards increasingly important to service providers?
choices: Providers can hire fewer staff when customers define standards.
Customers call frequently to discuss standards.
They link customer expectations and company actions.
Providers want customers to define standards when they can't think of any.
explanation: They link customer expectations and company actions. Customer-defined service standards are at the heart of delivery of service that customers expect. While it is important that service providers set quality measures, customer-defined service standards bring together what customers have said they want in the way of service delivery and what the provider will do to satisfy those expectations. Customer-defined service standards are important not because customers call to discuss them, but because they tell the provider (with their wallets) when their expectations are being met and when they aren't! Customer-defined service standards aren't an alternative to provider-defined standards but, instead, should be at the core of everything the providers do. Customer-defined service standards do not necessarily mean fewer staff for service providers. In fact, the opposite is probably true. Once providers understand what their customer expects, they may need additional resources, including staff, to deliver on those expectations.

prompt: Carol would rather have Dr. Jones examine her teeth, but will allow Dr. Smith to examine them if Dr. Jones is not available. In the services industry, this is an example of brand
explanation: Preference. Brand preference is the level of brand loyalty in which customers desire one brand over another but will accept substitutes if the brand is not available. In this instance, Dr. Jones is the preferred "brand" to Dr. Smith, although Dr. Smith is an acceptable alternative. Brand insistence is the level of brand loyalty in which customers will accept only one brand. Brand recognition is the level of brand loyalty in which customers are aware of a brand but not necessarily through personal experience. Responsiveness is not a level of brand loyalty.

prompt: Customers who base their perceptions of service quality on a service business's brochures and its employees' appearance are assessing the business by focusing on the _______ dimension.
explanation: Tangible. Service customers base their perceptions about a business's service quality by considering a combination of factors or quality dimensions. One factor is the tangible element of a service business. Tangible elements are those that the customer can taste, see, hear, smell, and touch. Since services are intangible products, customers often consider tangible factors such as the appearance of the business's facilities, employees, and promotional materials, such as brochures, to assess service quality. For example, a customer is less likely to buy dry cleaning services from a business that has shabby facilities and employees wearing food-stained clothing. Reliability is a quality dimension that relates to the business's dependability. Responsiveness is a quality dimension that encompasses efficiency and timing. Assurance is a quality dimension that addresses security and competency issues.

prompt: Why is it important for businesses to establish and implement effective service recovery procedures?
explanation: To keep existing customers. Service recovery involves handling problems caused by a failure to deliver services correctly. When customers do not receive services as promised, they usually complain and expect the business to make it right. If the business responds promptly and corrects the problem or satisfies the customer's concerns, it usually is able to recover from the failure and keep the customer. However, if the business does not have procedures in place to handle the service failure, it may lose customers who are dissatisfied. Effective service recovery procedures are intended to handle complaints and correct problems rather than to eliminate complaints. Businesses do not establish and maintain effective service recovery procedures to reduce operating expenses or to maintain inventory levels.

prompt: When a hospital uses promotion to announce that a new health-care service will soon be available to consumers, they achieve the promotional objective of
explanation: Informing. Informing is providing basic facts. Informing consumers about new and existing services is one of the functions of promotion. Persuading is attempting to convince the customer to buy. Reminding keeps the customer from forgetting that an existing product is available. Selling is communication intended to influence purchase decisions.

prompt: The primary goal of institutional advertising is to
choices: create a certain image of the company.
build a reputation for a product.
create interest in a new product.
explanation: Create a certain image of the company. Institutional promotion can create favorable public attitudes which will benefit the company. Creating interest in a new product, informing consumers about product features, and building a reputation for a product are goals of product promotion.

prompt: One of the advantages to service businesses of using a communication medium made possible by advanced technology to promote products is that the medium is
explanation: Interactive. One of the advantages of using the new communication technology to promote products is that it is interactive, thereby allowing service businesses to deal directly with consumers. Many businesses use the technology to create web sites that contain features that allow users to provide comments or ask questions. Other businesses use advertising kiosks that provide information or print coupons for customers at the touch of a finger. Other types of interactive communication include CD-ROMs and online magazines. Disadvantages of the new communication technology are that it is not standardized, is unregulated, and is expensive.

prompt: The broadcast medium that is most affordable and can reach an entire metropolitan area is
explanation: Radio. The production costs of a radio commercial and air time are relatively inexpensive, especially when compared to television. Radio is often used as a supplementary medium to reinforce a firm's other promotional efforts. Newspapers and magazines are both print media.

prompt: The advantage to pet-grooming businesses of using direct marketing is that it is considered an effective
explanation: Promotional tool. Direct marketing involves the use of one or more advertising media to communicate with the consumer. It is considered an effective promotional tool because it reaches the specific customer, or group of customers, that the business wants to target. For example, a pet-grooming business can send a sales flyer to a customer and follow it up with an e-mail to the same customer. The direct contact promotes the pet-grooming business and its services. A sales presentation is the sales procedure in which the salesperson shows the customer the benefits of the product's features. A transaction method is a way of handling a business activity, such as a sale, a purchase, or a return. The use of direct marketing does not necessarily save the business time.

prompt: The dry cleaner's advertisement included statements from customers praising the company's service and reasonable prices. What type of advertising approach was the dry cleaner using?
explanation: Testimonial. Advertising copy sometimes includes statements from people about their experiences with goods and services that are known as testimonials. This type of advertising is designed to promote the benefits of a product from the consumer's point of view. Comparisons are used to compare the features of competitive products. Hard-sell is an advertising approach that emphasizes urgency and often uses phrases such as "limited time" and "act now." Feature copy provides factual information about the product.

prompt: Which of the following is one of the reasons why child-care facilities coordinate promotional activities:
explanation: To create interest among customers. One of the main reasons for coordinating promotional activities is to create enough interest among customers that they will want to visit the child-care facility. Coordinated advertising, special events, and other promotions are designed to create in customers the desire to purchase goods and services. Collecting demographic information, developing long-term forecasts, and planning inventory control programs are not purposes of coordinating promotional activities.

prompt: When a professional-services firm considers how it will promote its products, it is determining how to
choices: maximize the number of visitors to its web site.
increase foot traffic at various trade shows.
draw attention to its pricing strategies.
explanation: Communicate information about its services. A service business is a type of business that performs intangible activities that satisfy the needs and wants of consumers or industrial users. Promotion is the marketing function that businesses use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of their products. Advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, and publicity are types of promotion that service-businesses use to communicate product information. Web sites, trade shows, and pricing discounts (sales) are vehicles that businesses use to communicate information about their products.

prompt: Customers are more likely to trust service businesses and their products when the salespeople are
explanation: Self-confident. A salesperson's confidence gives customers confidence in the service business. They feel that the company will stand by its promises and that they have made a good buying decision. Customers often do not respond well to salespeople who are aggressive, talkative, or insistent.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a salesperson providing poor customer service:
choices: Ignoring a customer's request for information
Returning a customer's call in a timely manner
Following up with a customer after the purchase
explanation: Ignoring a customer's request for information. Salespeople who do not provide good service are more likely to offend customers, which often results in a lost sale. Customers are less likely to return to the business if they feel that the salesperson is rude, lacks product knowledge, or ignores a request for information. When salespeople return calls in a timely manner, answer questions honestly, and conduct follow-up activities, customers are receiving good customer service and are likely to purchase from the business again.

prompt: Salespeople can show that they are giving customers their full attention by
explanation: Having an interested expression. When meeting with customers, conscientious salespeople offer their full attention and respect. They never interrupt the client, and the expression they display is one of interest. They show a sense of humor by making a few jokes and/or laughing at customers' jokes. They display tact by not discussing religion and politics. Doing favors for customers helps to build a clientele but is not an indication of paying close attention.

prompt: Which of the following can cause a car rental agency's profits to decrease:
choices: A salesperson offers a discount to a friend.
A competitor speaks highly of the company's services.
The company avoids incurring legal costs.
explanation: A salesperson offers a discount to a friend. Offering discounts to friends (often in violation of company policy or manager's instructions) can cause business profits to decrease. An increase in customer purchases and the avoidance of legal costs would likely have a positive effect on profits. A competitor's comment, whether positive or negative, may not have any effect on business profits.

prompt: What cost-effective tool is often used by salespeople who sell time-share plans and provide product information to customers that they can view on personal computers?
explanation: Multimedia disks. The disks can be inserted in a computer so the customer can view product information such as catalogs, diagrams, specifications, and testimonials. Audio disks are not visual in nature. Transparencies are generally viewed with overhead projectors. Micro bite is not a legitimate term to describe a tool to view information on a personal computer.

prompt: A client asks a hair salon employee about the specific chemicals that the salon uses in hair color treatments. What is the employee's most reliable source of information?
explanation: Manufacturer's brochures. Manufacturer's brochures and publications are furnished by the manufacturer and usually are free. If needed, additional product information can be obtained by contacting the manufacturer. The hair color manufacturer is the best source of information because it actually makes the product for the hair salon to use when providing salon services such as coloring a client's hair. Customers, intermediaries, and salespeople are not the most reliable sources because they may not know the chemical makeup of the color treatment.

prompt: What should a business-services salesperson remember to do during the closing phase of the selling process?
explanation: Ask the customer to buy. The actual closing of a sale is something with which many salespeople have difficulty. Salespeople should remember that they will usually need to ask the customer to buy. Putting customers at ease, asking questions, and explaining services are steps in other phases of the selling process.

prompt: A car-rental agency with several customers waiting should serve those customers
choices: in the order of their arrival.
explanation: In the order of their arrival. When the car-rental agency is busy and several customers are waiting for attention, salespeople should wait on customers in the order of their arrival. However, the car-rental agency's salespeople should acknowledge customers as soon as possible without interrupting the selling process with the first customer. Customers should not be kept waiting while salespeople balance the cash register—this is done at closing. Salespeople should not serve customers out of order simply because they appear to be irritated or they interrupt with questions.

prompt: A salesperson asking "Are you saying that you like the darker colors for the exterior but prefer a light color for the interior?" is an example of a(n) __________ question.
explanation: Rephrasing. A rephrasing (interpretive) question is asked to check for understanding when the salesperson summarizes the customer's ideas in his/her own words. An assumptive question is used to check for understanding when the salesperson feels that s/he knows how the customer will respond. An open-ended question requires more than a simple "yes" or "no" response. Beneficial is not a type of question.

prompt: When customers try to conceal the real reason for not buying, they are using a(n)
explanation: Excuse. An excuse is an insincere and invalid statement used to cover up a real reason for not buying. An objection is a point of difference between a customer and a salesperson that may prevent a sale. A testimonial is a method of handling objections in which the salesperson uses a neutral third party who has tried the product as an example. The inquiry is another method of handling objections in which the salesperson asks questions of customers to enable customers to answer their own objections.

prompt: Suggestion selling is important to business-services salespeople primarily because
choices: it increases total sales and possibly commissions.
it prepares them to operate their own service business.
the more business-services salespeople sell, the more they enjoy the job.
of the opportunity to make important contacts with people.
explanation: It increases total sales and possibly commissions. Suggestion selling increases total sales and profits for the service business, which may mean higher wages or commissions for the salesperson. Increasing sales may or may not increase the business-services salesperson's enjoyment of the job. Contacts with people can come whether or not you sell them something. Qualifications for running one's own service business involve much more than the ability to sell successfully. Such things as the ability to raise capital and proper understanding of other phases of business are also needed.

prompt: By probing, a salesperson should be able to determine a customer's
explanation: Buying motives. These are the reasons or benefits that cause people to purchase products. Once the salesperson has determined the customer's reason(s) for buying, s/he should be able to offer solutions or ideas that the company or its product(s) can provide. The salesperson should not attempt to determine the customer's disposable income, the amount the customer has left to spend after taxes. Social responsibility is the duty of business to contribute to the well-being of society. Fiscal policy is a government policy that sets levels of government spending and taxation.

prompt: Even a successful service business might have trouble maintaining consistent quality control measures over time because
choices: its employees' performance levels can vary.
consumers tend to develop brand loyalty.
explanation: Its employees' performance levels can vary. Quality is the degree of excellence of a product. Service businesses use standards to try to maintain and control service quality so service performance and delivery is consistent. Because employees are different, their performance levels often vary, which makes it more difficult for service businesses to maintain consistent quality control for their product delivery and performance. Economic conditions and brand loyalty are external factors that do not necessarily influence how a business manages its quality control measures. Most successful service businesses make some changes to their product mix over time and they revise their quality control measures to accommodate the changes.

prompt: John says that his job duties include planning what will be done, organizing and directing workers, and solving problems related to worker productivity. His job can best be described as a
explanation: Manager. Managers are responsible for organizing, planning, staffing, directing, and controlling the business's activities in order to reach certain goals. Bookkeepers and cashiers have other types of job responsibilities that usually do not include managing. Brokers act as agents for businesses and often negotiate purchases in exchange for a fee.
